evidence: The step coverage of the presented ALD processes was confirmed by SEM measurements on cross-sections of coated TSV structures. The electrical characterization of as-deposited Al2O3 ALD films using planar metal–insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors with titanium based electrodes proofed low leakage currents of less than 0.1 nA/cm2 at 2 MV/cm and high breakdown field strengths of about 7 MV/cm. Furthermore, metal insulator silicon (MIS) test structures with 15 nm Al2O3 films (annealed for 1 h at 300 /C176Ci nH2/N2) have been successfully tested on their copper diffusion barrier properties by means of bias temperature stress (BTS) - 30 min at 250 /C176C with an applied electric field of 2 MV/cm - followed by triangular voltage sweep (TVS) measurements. The ALD process for the ruthenium seed layer was enhanced by an intermediate annealing step improving film adhesion on the subjacent TaN-based diffusion barrier. The applied film thicknesses were chosen to allow reliable characterization using SEM cross-sections. The shown stack deposited without leaving the vacuum system implied a 10 nm thin Ru ALD film which was deposited earlier as a decoration to distinguish between the Si substrate and a following 100 nm thick Al2O3 insulating liner. The subsequent amorphous 32 nm TaN-based copper diffusion barrier was finally covered by a 33 nm polycrystalline Ru ALD film - as measured by in situ SE and confirmed by SEM - serving as seed layer for copper ECD. The result of the ECD process on the film stack described above shown in Fig. 7 B confirms the proper function of the Ru seed layer down to the bottom of the via and demonstrates the potential of the ALD approach for high aspect ratio copper-based TSVs.
